title: The Lion and the Mouse
summary: A mighty lion lets a little mouse go. Unexpectedly, one day that mouse is the one who saves him.
moral: Kindness is repaid with kindness, and no creature is too small to help a great one.
pages: Under a shady tree, the Lion, king of the forest, slept soundly. His snoring could be heard far away, and all the animals tiptoed so as not to wake him.
A little mouse, playing, accidentally ran across the Lion's nose. The Lion woke with a start, angry, and caught the mouse with his big paw. 'Who dares disturb my sleep?' he growled.
'Forgive me, King of the Forest!' begged the trembling Mouse. 'Let me go. One day I will surely repay your kindness.' The Lion was amazed. How could such a tiny mouse help the king of the forest?
The Lion laughed out loud. 'Very well, I will spare you. Go!' The little Mouse thanked him again and again, then ran home with a light heart.
A few days later, the Lion was caught in a net set by a hunter. He struggled and roared as loudly as he could, but the more he moved, the tighter the net bound him.
The little Mouse heard the roar and ran over at once. 'Calm down, King of the Forest, I will help you!' Nibble, nibble, nibble! He bit through the ropes of the net one by one until they all broke.
The Lion was free! 'Thank you, Mouse. I was wrong to look down on you,' he said sincerely. From that day on they were friends. The Lion learned that kindness is never wasted. The end.
